Britain's Best Motorcycle-Accessible Viewpoints

Some viewpoints require hours of hillwalking. These don't. Every viewpoint on this list is accessible by motorcycle — park up, take off your helmet, and drink in views that will stay with you forever. We've picked the most spectacular overlooks in Scotland, England, and Wales that you can ride right to.

Scotland

  • Bealach na Bà Summit (Applecross Pass): At 2,054ft, the summit car park offers a staggering panorama across to Skye, Raasay, and the Outer Hebrides. On a clear day, you can see the Cuillins. There's a proper parking area where your bike is safe.
  • Quiraing Viewpoint, Skye: The single-track road across the Trotternish Ridge offers views so dramatic they've been used in multiple Hollywood films. Park at the Quiraing car park and the view unfolds before you.
  • Rest and Be Thankful, Argyll: The A83 climbs through Glen Croe to the Rest and Be Thankful pass. The viewpoint car park overlooks the glen below — a classic Highland vista.
  • Cairn o' Mount, Aberdeenshire: The B974 crosses the Mounth at 1,488ft. The summit viewpoint offers a vast panorama across Deeside and the Cairngorms. Easy parking.
  • Duncansby Head, Caithness: The true northeastern tip of mainland Britain. Park at the lighthouse and walk five minutes to the sea stacks — dramatic sandstone pillars rising from the ocean.

England

  • Hartside Summit, North Pennines: At 1,904ft on the A686, the Hartside Café viewpoint looks across the Eden Valley to the Lake District fells. A legendary biker stop.
  • Sutton Bank, North York Moors: The viewpoint at the top of the A170 escarpment gives a vast westward view across the Vale of York. On clear days, you can see the Pennines 40 miles away.
  • Devil's Bridge, Lake District: The old bridge over the River Lune near Kirkby Lonsdale. Ruskin called the view from here one of the finest in England. Park in the village and walk two minutes.
  • Winnats Pass, Peak District: The narrow pass is a viewpoint in itself — towering limestone cliffs on either side. The parking area at the western end gives dramatic upward views.
  • Beachy Head, East Sussex: England's highest chalk cliffs at 530ft. Ride right to the clifftop car park for dizzying views down to the lighthouse and across the English Channel.

Wales

  • Pen-y-Pass, Snowdonia: At the top of the Llanberis Pass, the car park offers views down the pass towards Llyn Padarn and across to the Glyderau. Arrive early — it fills up fast in summer.
  • Gospel Pass, Black Mountains: The highest road pass in Wales at 1,778ft. The summit overlook gives panoramic views across the Black Mountains and the Wye Valley.
  • Great Orme, Llandudno: A toll road climbs the Great Orme headland. From the summit, views extend across Snowdonia, Anglesey, and the Irish Sea.
The best viewpoints are often the ones you discover by accident — a lay-by on a mountain road, a gap in the hedge revealing the sea, a bridge crossing a river valley. Keep your eyes open and stop whenever something catches your eye. That's what touring is for.

Photography Tips at Viewpoints

  • Park your bike in the foreground of the view for a classic touring photo
  • Visit at golden hour (first or last light) for the most dramatic images
  • Include the road curving away into the distance — it tells the story of the ride
  • Take photos with and without the bike — sometimes the landscape deserves to stand alone

These viewpoints are the punctuation marks of a great motorcycle tour — the moments where you stop, breathe, and remember why you ride.

Essential Snowdonia Stops

Beddgelert is one of Wales's prettiest villages, nestled where two rivers meet beneath wooded hills. Stop for tea at one of the village cafes and stretch your legs along the riverside walk. The Sygun Copper Mine nearby offers underground tours that make a unique mid-ride diversion.

The Ogwen Valley between Capel Curig and Bethesda is another highlight — Llyn Ogwen sits beneath the dramatic Tryfan peak, and the road through the valley is tight and technical. The Zip World sites at Bethesda and Blaenau Ffestiniog offer adrenaline stops if you fancy something different between riding sessions. Don't overlook the area around Bala and Llyn Tegid — Wales's largest natural lake with quiet roads circling it and good facilities for fuel and food in the town.

Where to Stay

Betws-y-Coed is the traditional base for Snowdonia motorcycle touring, with good fuel, accommodation, and restaurants. Beddgelert is quieter and prettier — one of Wales's most charming villages. Dolgellau at the southern end of the park gives access to Cadair Idris and the Mawddach Estuary. All three have biker-friendly B&Bs and nearby campsites. For food, the Ty Gwyn Hotel in Betws-y-Coed serves excellent Welsh lamb, and the fish and chips at The Big Rock Café in Porthmadog are legendary among touring riders. The national park visitor centres at Betws-y-Coed and Beddgelert provide maps, weather updates, and local road condition information. keyTakeaways: Every viewpoint here is reachable by bike, from the Bealach na Ba summit car park to Beachy Head's clifftop.
Scotland's best include Bealach na Ba, the Quiraing on Skye, and Duncansby Head near John o' Groats.
England's classics are Hartside Summit, Sutton Bank, and Winnats Pass in the Peak District.
Wales delivers Pen-y-Pass, Gospel Pass at 1,778ft, and the Great Orme toll road above Llandudno.
Visit at golden hour and park your bike in the foreground for the classic touring photograph.

faq.q: Can I park my bike safely at these viewpoints?
faq.a: Most have proper car parks or lay-bys where a motorcycle sits securely, including the Bealach na Ba summit, Hartside, Sutton Bank, and Beachy Head. Pen-y-Pass and the Quiraing fill quickly in summer, so arrive early. Park on firm, level ground, avoid soft verges that can sink a sidestand, and use your disc lock at busier tourist honeypots.

faq.q: When is the light best for viewpoint photography?
faq.a: Golden hour, the first and last hour of sunlight, gives warm, soft light and long shadows that flatter both the landscape and your bike. East-facing viewpoints like Sutton Bank shine at sunrise, while west-facing spots such as the Bealach na Ba come alive at sunset. Scattered cloud often produces more dramatic skies than a completely clear day.

faq.q: Which viewpoints need a short walk from parking?
faq.a: Several reward a brief stroll. Duncansby Head is a five-minute walk from the lighthouse car park to the sea stacks, and Devil's Bridge near Kirkby Lonsdale is two minutes from the village. The Quiraing viewpoint is right by its car park. Wear grippy footwear rather than smooth-soled riding boots for any path near cliffs or uneven ground.

faq.q: Are the Scottish summit viewpoints accessible all year?
faq.a: Not reliably. The Bealach na Ba closes in severe winter weather, and high roads to viewpoints like Cairn o' Mount can be blocked by snow or ice from late autumn into spring. Check conditions before setting out in the colder months. Summer offers the safest access but the busiest car parks, so early starts pay off.
